subject: Request: deletion evidence & clarification on default capture horizon for prompts vs final outputs
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@epsilonhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@epsilonhealth.com, infra@epsilonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence of deletion + what we should expect to be retained by default

Hi Jonas,

Quick one from our compliance and infra teams as we approach SOC onboarding next month. A couple of asks so we can close internal tickets: 

1) If a customer requests 'complete deletion' for a set of session ids, what evidence will Redwood provide that objects were removed? We need a human/audit-friendly artefact for legal.
2) Please confirm the "default capture horizon" for the following elements in hosted mode:
   - raw request (user prompt)
   - model response (finalized output)
   - streamed tokens / transient fragments / KV cache traces

We'd like an example export and an approximate SLA/time-to-purge after an erase request. Attached is our deletion matrix that lists what Redwood asked in the questionnaire (epsilon_deletion_request_20260921.pdf).

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Kim
Head of Compliance, Epsilon Health

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@epsilonhealth.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence of deletion + what we should expect to be retained by default

Sara — thanks for the clear asks, and appreciate the attachment. High level answers first, then I've looped Mina (engineering) for the export example and Kimberly (security/legal ops) for the audit/evidence language.

High level:
- Evidence: We provide a deletion audit package containing the deletion job id(s), object keys / record ids removed, S3 lifecycle event snapshots (when applicable), and the job run logs. That package is a human-readable CSV plus a short JSON manifest that ties deletion IDs to HubSpot ticket ids.
- Default capture horizon (hosted):
  * Raw request (prompt): default capture window = 45 days. Prompts are flagged as request artifacts and eligible for auto-prune after the window unless customer enables longer retention or export.
  * Model response (finalized output): default capture window = 90 days for debugging/quality monitoring; note customers can opt out of storing generated outputs at account level.
  * Streamed tokens / fragments / KV cache traces: considered ephemeral. Streaming fragments and transient KV cache entries are not persisted to long-term storage by default; they are kept in memory or short-lived buffers and flushed within minutes.

SLA for erasure requests: standard hosted erase actions are scheduled within 48 hours and completed within 7 days for typical workloads. Enterprise/contracted SLAs can be faster and can include a signed deletion certificate.

Mina — can you attach a sample export snippet (anonymized) that shows the deletion manifest format? Kimberly — please add recommended wording for a deletion certificate we can provide to Epsilon's legal team.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@epsilonhealth.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence of deletion + what we should expect to be retained by default

Hi Sara — attaching a short, redacted export snippet to show the fields we include in the deletion package.

Attachment: export_snippet_soc2_20260921.csv (CSV text)
  - columns we include: deletion_job_id, record_id, object_key, created_at, removed_at, removal_action (auto_prune|manual_erase), note
  - sample row: JID-20260921-7a9, REC-8f3c, s3://redwood-prod/requests/2026/09/rec-8f3c.json, 2026-07-03T12:11:22Z, 2026-09-21T12:45:02Z, manual_erase, "requested via support ticket #EPS-4821"

A couple of technical clarifications:
- "Finalized outputs" are written to our persistent store only after model response finalization; intermediate streaming fragments are buffered and not persisted.
- We maintain mapping metadata (record_id -> hash(prompt)) for a short diagnostic window; the system can match a submitted prompt to stored items for the retention window, but we do not store raw prompts beyond the configured retention unless explicitly opted-in.
- On the backend we execute erasure via idempotent deletion jobs. Job logs include retry history; these are included in the audit bundle.

I'll also include the S3 lifecycle event id and the job run id in the manifest when we produce the customer bundle.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Engineer, Runtime Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@epsilonhealth.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence of deletion + what we should expect to be retained by default

Sara — adding the legal/ops wording you can include in your SOC artifact collection. This is a short template we provide to customers after an erase request: 

Deletion Certificate (sample wording):
"On 2026-09-21 Redwood Inference executed deletion job JID-20260921-7a9 for account Epsilon Health (acct-id: EPS-12345). The deletion job removed the listed record ids and corresponding object keys from our active storage and object indices. Attached are: (1) a CSV manifest of removed records, (2) a JSON manifest linking deletion job ids to HubSpot ticket ids, and (3) service-side job logs and lifecycle event ids. Retained backups and immutable forensic snapshots are subject to our standard retention policies and, where applicable, customer-configured retention controls. Evidence of removal from live indices is provided by the attached CSV and the job run logs."

Operational notes:
- If you require eradication from backups or forensic snapshots, that is treated as an exceptional request and requires a signed scope and additional SLAs. We can handle this under the Private deployment offering or via an enterprise contract addendum.
- For transparency: default horizons (45/90/ephemeral) are configurable at account level; we can flip the flag to opt-out of storing outputs entirely for your pilot.

If you confirm you want the standard hosted erasure + certificate, we'll open the erase job and provide the audit bundle when it's completed.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance Operations — Redwood Inference
